note: Fixed service choices per need, cloud and compute model. scripts/recommend.py reads this file so every run, with any model, picks the same services. Names and availability change; the web verification step in SKILL.md checks them against official vendor pages at run time.

server.why: Runs your containers continuously without you managing servers, so background workers and long-lived streaming connections keep working.

alternatives.reason: Adds Kubernetes you would have to operate; worth it only if you already run Kubernetes.

serverless.why: Runs your code per request and scales to zero, so you pay only when it is called.
serverless.caveat: Each invocation has a time limit, and streaming or WebSocket routes need extra setup.

alternatives.reason: Choose the server-based model if the app needs long-running work or streaming.

server.why: Runs your containers continuously with built-in HTTPS and scaling, without managing servers or Kubernetes.

alternatives.reason: Adds Kubernetes you would have to operate.

serverless.why: Runs your code per event or request and scales automatically, so you pay for use.
serverless.caveat: Execution time limits depend on the hosting plan, and streaming routes need testing.

alternatives.reason: Choose the server-based model if the app needs long-running work or streaming.

server.why: Runs your containers continuously with built-in HTTPS and autoscaling, without managing servers.

serverless.why: Runs your containers per request and scales to zero when idle, so you pay for use and web frameworks run unchanged.
serverless.caveat: The first request after an idle period starts a container, which adds a short delay, and request time limits apply.

alternatives.reason: Function-style deployment without a container, but the app has to be restructured into functions.

server.why: Receives HTTPS traffic in public subnets and forwards it to containers in private subnets, so the containers are never exposed to the internet.

alternatives.reason: Works at the connection level and does not route by URL path.

serverless.why: Gives the functions a managed HTTPS front door with throttling and authentication hooks.

alternatives.reason: Can also front Lambda; API Gateway adds API keys and quotas.

server.why: Terminates HTTPS in front of private containers and routes by URL path.

alternatives.reason: Works at the connection level and does not route by URL path.

alternatives.reason: Simpler if you only need routing and a firewall.
